title: SuperMAN: Interpretable and Expressive Networks over Temporally Sparse Heterogeneous Data
claim: Heterogeneous inputs are encoded per group, aggregated hierarchically through set-level pooling, and summed into a single interpretable prediction.
layout: Single row, left-to-right, three input groups merging via arrows into one label
description: A left-to-right flow diagram. At the left are two rounded colored boxes: a purple box S1 containing two small node-link graphs, G1 and G2, and a green box S2 containing one graph, G3. Each graph feeds an arrow into a rounded module. The purple graphs go to ExtGNAN 1 and the green graph goes to ExtGNAN 2, and each module is the same color as its input box. Each module outputs a small segmented cylinder, labeled Graph Representations. The two purple vectors converge on a gray DeepSet block, which outputs a hatched Subset Representation vector. A long arrow carries the green vector straight across without aggregation. Both reach a gray Vector Sum block, which outputs an orange Final Set Representation. That goes to a gray Entry-Sum block and then to a Label output. The eye lands first on the colored input boxes, then follows the arrows to the right.
caption: In this example, the input is a set of three graphs, $G_1, G_2, G_3$, grouped into two subsets $S_1$ and $S_2$. Within each subset, the same ExtGNAN instance is applied to all graphs to produce their graph-level representations. For subsets containing multiple graphs, a DeepSets module aggregates these graph representations into a single subset representation. For subsets of size one, the subset representation is simply the graph representation itself. The final set representation is then obtained by summing the subset representations, and the final label prediction is produced by summing the entries of this set representation.
abstract: Real-world temporal data often consists of multiple signal types recorded at irregular, asynchronous intervals. For instance, in the medical domain, different types of blood tests can be measured at different times and frequencies, resulting in fragmented and unevenly scattered temporal data. Similar issues of irregular sampling occur in other domains, such as the monitoring of large systems using event log files. Effectively learning from such data requires handling sets of temporal sparse and heterogeneous signals. In this work, we propose Super Mixing Additive Networks (SuperMAN), a novel and interpretable-by-design framework for learning directly from such heterogeneous signals, by modeling them as sets of implicit graphs. SuperMAN provides diverse interpretability capabilities, including node-level, graph-level, and subset-level importance, and enables practitioners to trade finer-grained interpretability for greater expressivity when domain priors are available. SuperMAN achieves state-of-the-art performance in real-world high-stakes tasks, including predicting Crohn's disease onset and hospital length of stay from routine blood test measurements and detecting fake news. Furthermore, we demonstrate how SuperMAN's interpretability properties assist in revealing disease development phase transitions and provide crucial insights in the healthcare domain.
